definitions.explanation: The day with the shortest period of daylight and the longest night of the year, occurring around December 21-22 in the Northern Hemisphere. In Japan, it is traditionally associated with eating kabocha squash and taking yuzu baths.

examples.japanese: ⟦{今年|ことし}→今年：00722_kotoshi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{冬至|とうじ}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧12⟦{月|がつ}→月：30418_gatsu⟧22⟦{日|にち}→日：12732_nichi⟧だ。
examples.english: This year's winter solstice is December 22nd.

examples.japanese: {冬至|とうじ}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦かぼちゃ→かぼちゃ：10306_kabocha⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{食|た}べる→食べる：00396_taberu⟧⟦{習慣|しゅうかん}→習慣：01429_shuukan⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧。
examples.english: There is a custom of eating kabocha squash on the winter solstice.

examples.japanese: {冬至|とうじ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{過|す}ぎる→過ぎる：01219_sugiru⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧、⟦{少|すこ}し→少し：00596_sukoshi⟧⟦ずつ→〜ずつ：03092_zutsu⟧⟦{日|ひ}→日：02249_hi⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{長|なが}く→長い：00491_nagai⟧⟦なって→なる：01970_naru⟧いく。
examples.english: After the winter solstice, the days gradually get longer.

notes:
The shortest day and longest night of the year, occurring around December 21-22 in Japan.

JAPANESE CUSTOMS:
- ⟦{柚子|ゆず}→柚子：13102_yuzu⟧⟦{湯|ゆ}→湯：01740_yu⟧: taking a bath with yuzu citrus fruit, believed to ward off illness
- ⟦かぼちゃ→かぼちゃ：10306_kabocha⟧: eating kabocha squash for good health and good luck
- Traditionally, eating foods with "ん" in the name on this day brings luck

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {冬至|とうじ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{日|ひ}→日：02249_hi⟧: the day of the winter solstice
- {冬至|とうじ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{迎|むか}える→迎える：01193_mukaeru⟧: to reach the winter solstice
- {冬至|とうじ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{過|す}ぎる→過ぎる：01219_sugiru⟧: to pass the winter solstice

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{夏至|げし}→夏至：19819_geshi⟧: summer solstice (longest day)
- ⟦{春分|しゅんぶん}→春分：19942_shunbun⟧: spring equinox
- ⟦{秋分|しゅうぶん}→秋分：19657_shuubun⟧: autumn equinox
